All five scenarios hold, so I wrote `{"findings": []}` to `openspec/changes/308-steer-dead-task/.run/validator/findings.json`. I only read the code and tests; I ran no build, test or git command.

- **status-inspection: Dead task without a trigger, Run triggers win, Nothing died.** The new `humanSteering` in `src/core/status/steering.ts:175` returns the existing run triggers if there are any. Otherwise it returns one `dead` trigger for each dead task. `tests/steering-dead-plan.test.ts` checks each THEN directly. These tests can't pass on the base code because `humanSteering` doesn't exist there.
- **cli-foundation: Plan a dead task in its worktree.** For worktree changes, `readSteeringPlan` now uses `humanSteering`. When every trigger is `dead`, the section opens with `A task of this change died, and a human asked to revise its plan.` The existing `triggerLines` code adds the `### task 2 dead (timeout)` heading, the marker path as `Evidence: …` and the marker body. The `Done tasks stay done: 1.` line comes from the existing code too. The test checks all of these, plus that the checkout holds no copy and that no new change folder appears. On the base code `state.steering` is unset here, so the command fails with `needs no steering` and the test would fail.
- **spec-lint-and-approve: Dead task approved again in its worktree.** `approveSpec` now calls the new `worktreeNeedsSteering`, which sends the case to `approveSteeredChange`. That function makes the `osq: <id> approved` commit, then calls `retireSteering`, which runs `retrySpec` on task 2 to move the dead marker aside. The test in `tests/steering-dead-approve.test.ts` checks every item in the THEN. On the base code `state.steering` is undefined, so the steered-approval branch is never taken and the test would fail.
